title: Connplex Zoning Studio — Rules & Config Registry
description: Central, versioned, source-backed rule/catalogue data. Application and layout-engine code must read these values, never hardcode them (Master Context Product Principle #1 / §74-75). Every value below carries an approval_status; only DECIDED / SOURCE_BACKED entries may act as production hard constraints. ENGINEERING_ASSUMPTION entries are clearly marked and must not be silently promoted.

sources.note: Image-based PDF; exact figures should be re-verified against the scan before promoting a value to a stricter status.

sources.name: theater_architecture_complete_standards.csv (user-supplied, sourced from the public internet)
sources.org: Not Connplex-specific — cites SMPTE ST 290, THX Architecture Guidelines, British Standards BS 5588, ASHRAE, and several U.S. legal codes (IBC, NFPA 101, ADA, IPC)
sources.note: The U.S. legal-code citations (IBC/NFPA/ADA/IPC) are NOT verified against India's National Building Code or the local cinema-licensing rules that actually govern Connplex's real projects (Gujarat, Maharashtra per this app's own project records) — only jurisdiction-agnostic engineering/design conventions from this source were wired in as rules; the rest are listed in not_evaluable_today with the reason.

sources.name: Cinema_Layout_Notes.pdf (client-provided operational notes)
sources.note: A working notes document the client sent directly (2026-09-10) covering component placement order/issues and a table of minimum-area limits per support-zone type. Treated as the primary source of truth for the client's own operational minimums where no formal SOP figure existed or where it explicitly supersedes an earlier unsourced engineering placeholder.

seat_types.name: Front Lounger
seat_types.min_row_step_display: ≈ 5'-8" (derived from 68in side-elevation length — same derivation PREMIUM_RECLINER already uses for its own row step; NOT an explicit SOP row-step figure)
seat_types.notes: Reclines with leg-rest extension; row step not explicitly given in SOP extract, estimated from its own stated footprint instead of left unusable.

seat_types.name: Recliner / Lounger (generic)
seat_types.notes: Generic entry in source table with no footprint dims — do not use for area/seat-count math until disambiguated against a named SKU.

seat_types.name: Premium Recliner
seat_types.min_row_step_display: ≈ 5'-9" (derived from 69in open depth; NOT an explicit SOP row-step figure)

seat_types.name: Duo Premium Recliner (Primus)
seat_types.notes: Individual recline switches, shared armrest enclosure.

seat_types.name: Duo Recliner Lounger (Lunar Lounger)
seat_types.notes: Chaise-style with ottoman; row step not stated in source.

auditorium_presets.name: 35-seat premium auditorium
auditorium_presets.source_section: Derived from an actual executed Connplex zoning deliverable (client file 'IINFINITY FF (1).dwg', not the SOP document): Screen 1 measured 959.3 sqft / 24.7x38.9ft seating 34 (Premium Recliner), Screen 4 measured 928.2 sqft / 26.4x35.2ft seating 34 across 17 Duo Lounger units. Added because the registry's smallest existing preset (60_SEAT, 1350 sqft / 30ft min width) is larger than either of these two real, already-built screens — the auto-layout generator could not have reproduced this real design without a smaller tier. Numbers are direct measurements from that file, not invented, but the preset itself (its exact width/length bounds and which seat types belong in it) hasn't been reviewed against the SOP the way the other three have.

franchise_tiers.name: Express
franchise_tiers.naming_conflict_note: Brochure calls this tier 'Express'; the ROI spreadsheet calls the equivalent tier 'Smart'. RESOLVED (user decision, 2026-09-01, spec §10 Open Item #2): 'Express' is the canonical client-facing name; 'Smart' is kept only as a known alias (see aka above) for anyone cross-referencing the ROI sheet.

support_zone_defaults.name: Box Office / Ticketing
support_zone_defaults.notes: Must be immediately visible on arrival from the lift/main entry (see the BOX_OFFICE sightline preference in _support_zone_heuristic). Minimum confirmed unchanged against the client's own notes; may be sized up beyond this default.

support_zone_defaults.name: Foyer
support_zone_defaults.notes: Manually-placed public lobby zone (Box Office/Waiting/F&B/Washrooms/Electrical/Server/Store per FOYER_REQUIRED_FUNCTIONS) — sized against the franchise tier's passage_to_screen_ratio when a tier is set, or 30% of auditorium area otherwise; this is only the hard floor. Note: this is the room type the app calls FOYER as of 2026-09-10 — before that date the same manually-placed room type was called PASSAGE and the derived-leftover concept was called FOYER; the two names were swapped at the client's explicit request once the terminology mismatch was found.

support_zone_defaults.name: Food & Beverage / Concession
support_zone_defaults.notes: Target still defaults to 8% of usable area (Master Context Sec 35 illustrative figure, not a decided rule) — only the minimum is client-sourced.

support_zone_defaults.name: Back-of-House (Electrical / Server)
support_zone_defaults.notes: SOP lists these as required foyer sub-functions but gives no area figures. 'Store' dropped from the display name — STORE_ROOM is now its own room type below, client-sourced, so it no longer double-counts the same physical space under BOH.

support_zone_defaults.name: Electrical Room
support_zone_defaults.notes: Was an unsourced REQUIRES_APPROVAL placeholder (40 sqft) deliberately excluded from SUPPORT_ZONE_AUTO_ORDER 'until a real figure exists' — the client's notes now supply one. Left excluded from SUPPORT_ZONE_AUTO_ORDER regardless: the client's notes gave an area figure, not a request to change auto-placement inclusion.

support_zone_defaults.name: Projector Room
support_zone_defaults.notes: Was an unsourced REQUIRES_APPROVAL placeholder (60 sqft) deliberately excluded from SUPPORT_ZONE_AUTO_ORDER 'until a real figure exists' — the client's notes now supply one. Left excluded from SUPPORT_ZONE_AUTO_ORDER regardless (see ELECTRICAL note).

support_zone_defaults.name: Store Room
support_zone_defaults.notes: New room type, split out of BOH's prior combined 'Electrical/Server/Store' description — the client's notes give Store Room its own distinct minimum.

support_zone_defaults.name: Passage / Corridor
support_zone_defaults.notes: This is the derived-leftover-remainder room (never independently placed — see layout_engine._build_passage_room and main.py._replace_passage_with_derived), computed as whatever's genuinely left once every other room is placed. Minimum used as a real-area viability check, not a placement target. Note: this is the room type the app calls PASSAGE as of 2026-09-10 — see the FOYER entry above for the same terminology-swap history.

planning_norms.description: First-row distance >= screen width. Now evaluable: intake captures screen_width_ft, and seat_engine.estimate_seats() uses max(SCREEN_TO_BACK_WALL_MIN_FT, screen_width_ft) as the effective front setback so the seat-packing math satisfies this by construction whenever screen_width_ft is provided — see viability rule VR_FIRST_ROW_DISTANCE.
Wall-to-seat side clearance used by the v1 seat-packing estimator. NOT stated explicitly in the SOP extract available to this project.
Rear circulation clearance used by the v1 seat-packing estimator. NOT stated explicitly in the SOP extract available to this project.

Minimum share of a region's usable area (after auditoriums) the v1 auto-layout keeps as genuine circulation rather than growing support zones (foyer/F&B/washroom/box office/BOH) into it. No SOP-stated circulation percentage exists for this pipeline; set from what a well-packed real floor plate looks like, not a claim of company policy.

Cap on how far a support zone's target area may grow past its formulaic target (see SUPPORT_ZONE_CIRCULATION_RESERVE_RATIO) when real leftover usable area is available, so no single zone balloons past what's architecturally plausible.
Foyer at main entry level must include these functions.

planning_norms.value: near plumbing shaft; not directly visible from foyer; easily accessible
planning_norms.description: Qualitative adjacency rule, not yet machine-checkable without a sightline model.

planning_norms.value: visible from entry; adequate circulation; plumbing lines available
no cross-movement between entry/exit flows; separate entry & exit flow per auditorium; direct fire-exit access from circulation

planning_norms.description: Measurable proxy threshold for SEPARATE_ENTRY_EXIT_FLOW's qualitative 'no cross-movement between entry/exit flows' rule: the straight-line distance below which a marked exit point is flagged as not clearly separated from the main entrance. The SOP states the qualitative rule but no specific distance; this is v1's own line-of-sight substitute for real circulation-path routing (which this engine does not model), so a warning, never a hard block, and revisable once real adjacency/path data exists.

Max share of a placed auditorium's own footprint a confirmed structural COLUMN may cover before the placement engine rejects that position and tries a different preset/spot. A column inside the seating bowl blocks sightlines and seats — real design routes around it, not through it — so this is deliberately near-zero, unlike the much more tolerant support-zone cap (see SUPPORT_ZONE_MAX_ENCLOSED_COLUMN_RATIO). Not stated in the SOP extract; set from first principles, not company policy.

Max share of a placed support zone's (foyer/F&B/box office/washroom/BOH/passage) own footprint a confirmed structural COLUMN may cover. Deliberately generous — real foyers and services cores commonly wrap a column or an entire lift/stair core (confirmed against two real Connplex reference floor plans in docs/reference/ during this feature's design pass), unlike an auditorium's seating bowl. Not stated in the SOP extract; set from first principles, not company policy.

Minimum clear width for a PASSAGE/CORRIDOR zone connecting the foyer to the auditoriums. Derived from a single real, observed measurement (a 2514mm-wide passage in a real Connplex reference floor plan, docs/reference/), not a code citation — distinct from CENTRAL_AISLE_MIN_FT, which governs the much narrower in-auditorium seating aisle, not a building egress corridor.

Clear width used for an auto-placed auditorium entry/exit door glyph — a real single-leaf-plus door width. Not stated in the SOP extract as a specific figure (SEPARATE_ENTRY_EXIT_FLOW states the qualitative requirement only); set from first principles, not company policy.

A confirmed structural COLUMN inside a placed auditorium is only tolerated (subject to AUDITORIUM_MAX_ENCLOSED_COLUMN_RATIO) when it falls within this distance of one of the room's own four walls — near enough to be absorbed into wall furring/an aisle. A column farther than this from every wall (stranded in the interior of the seating field) rejects the placement outright, regardless of how small its area share is, since it blocks sightlines wherever it sits. Matches PERIMETER_TOUCH_TOLERANCE_FT's existing 'near-the-edge' magnitude. Not stated in the SOP extract; set from first principles, not company policy.

Clear width used for an auto-placed support zone's (box office/F&B/washroom/BOH) single entry door glyph — a standard single-leaf commercial door, narrower than AUDITORIUM_DOOR_WIDTH_FT since these rooms don't carry the separate entry/exit flow requirement auditoriums do. Not stated in the SOP extract as a specific figure; set from first principles, not company policy.

Preferred maximum straight-line distance from the marked main entry point to a Box Office room's centroid. Both real reference floor plans (Keshav Landmark Vadodara, Maruti Nandan Dhule) show Box Office immediately beside the Cinema Entry/Exit, but no SOP document states a numeric threshold for how close is close enough — combined with the existing entry-sightline preference as a soft placement preference in _support_zone_heuristic, never a hard constraint. An unmeasured engineering guess, not a figure taken from either reference drawing.

How far along the seating-depth axis, on either side of a side-wall door's own span, the nearest seat (the one closest to that wall) is dropped from an auditorium's seat packing — a door swinging into the seating field displaces the seat(s) immediately beside it. Not stated as a specific figure in the SOP extract; set from the closest documented analog, AUDITORIUM_COLUMN_EDGE_TOLERANCE_FT (2.0ft), a comparable 'how close to an in-room obstruction can a seat legally sit' judgment.

viability_rules.message_template: Clear height below 10'-0" minimum — NOT VIABLE.
Structural column grid width below 20 ft absolute minimum — NOT VIABLE.
Structural column grid length below 30 ft absolute minimum — NOT VIABLE.
Seats per screen below the SOP's 55-60 layout-efficiency floor.
Seats per screen below the Pre-Deal Feasibility Manual's 60-seat/screen hard minimum.
Total project seats below the legal minimum of 175 (min 1, max 6 screens).
viability_rules.notes: Distinct from the per-screen design-efficiency floor above — do not merge (CLAUDE.md rule).
Not evaluable from current CAD extraction — no staircase classification in geometry model yet.

viability_rules.message_template: First-row-to-screen distance is shorter than the screen width — SOP §4.4/§9's first-row legibility rule.
viability_rules.notes: first_row_margin_ft is a derived measurement (first_row_distance_ft - screen_width_ft, min across placed auditoriums), computed in main.py._build_measurements — see FIRST_ROW_DISTANCE_RULE in planning_norms for the underlying formula. INSUFFICIENT_DATA when screen_width_ft isn't set or no auditorium is placed yet, same as every other not-yet-measurable rule.

viability_rules.message_template: Front margin below the 12 m preferred setback — verify against local DCR.
Side margin below 6 m minimum — must be verified against applicable local DCR.
Building height exceeds 50 ft (15.24 m) — requires DCR permission or competent-authority approval.
Back row is more than 120 ft from the screen — facial expression/legibility degrades past this distance.
viability_rules.source_section: Screen Placement & Layout / Last Row Distance

viability_rules.message_template: Combined support-zone area (everything except screens) is outside the client's own 30-40% target share of total usable area.
viability_rules.notes: support_zone_area_pct_of_carpet = (sum of every placed room's area_sqft where room_type does not start with AUDITORIUM, including the derived PASSAGE remainder) / total usable area * 100 — see main.py's measurement builder.

not_evaluable_today: clear_height_ft (not present in the current CAD extraction — intake field only, not geometry-derived)
column_grid_width_ft / column_grid_length_ft (structural grid spacing is not yet computed from extracted StructuralElement column positions)
fire_escape_staircase_count, passenger_lift_count, dg_backup_present (no CAD classification for these object types yet)

screen_bottom_elevation_ft, screen_curvature, sightline_c_value_in, floor_slope_pct (theater_architecture_complete_standards.csv, Screen Placement/Sightlines rows) — this app draws a 2D floor plan only; none of these are elevation/section quantities it computes or has any geometry for

noise_criterion_nc, wall_stc_rating, hvac_air_velocity_fpm (theater_architecture_complete_standards.csv, Acoustics & Isolation rows) — acoustic/MEP design values with no relationship to floor-plan geometry; out of this app's scope entirely

exit_count_vs_occupancy, egress_travel_distance_ft, restroom_fixture_ratio, ada_wheelchair_seat_pct (theater_architecture_complete_standards.csv, Entry & Exit / Amenities rows) — real, implementable checks in principle, but every cited source (IBC, NFPA 101, ADA, IPC) is a U.S. legal code; withheld pending confirmation these match (or should be replaced by) the actual code governing Connplex's real project locations before being wired in as feasibility gates
